title: TypeScript tracker client writes bytes tk would not, and its fixture test is hand-picked
description:
The TS tracker client emits tick JSON that differs from what tk itself writes, and the test that should catch this compares against hand-picked fixtures rather than against tk's own output.

This is the b9w failure shape returning: a second implementation of a shared format, and a test that cannot tell when the two diverge because it was written from the same misunderstanding as the code.

Work: generate the fixtures from tk rather than curating them, so the test fails when tk changes or when the client drifts.

From pxc, finding 7707a087.
acceptance_criteria: The tracker client's output is byte-compared against tk's own for a generated corpus, and the test fails if either side changes independently
